Stage 1 · Intro

Getting the details

Ask for detailed information — and check that you understood.

Stage 4 · Recall

Recall

Person words end in -er or -or. Choose the correct word.

Why

Stage 5 · Grammar

Grammar

Wh- questions — getting the details.
Track 3.7 — the question bankOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
1 Where do you live? 2 What do you usually wear to work? 3 Why do you want to learn English? 4 What time do you start work or class? 5 When do you take breaks? 6 Who do you live with? 7 What do you do when you're bored? 8 How often do you check your emails?
In other words
“Where do you live?”
“What time do you start work?”
“Who do you live with?”
“How often do you check your emails?”
Notice

Notice: what comes after the question word — and where is do / does?

Question wordQuestionAnswer
WhereWhere do you live?In Astana.
What timeWhat time does she start work?At nine.
WhoWho do you live with?With my parents.
How oftenHow often does he travel?Twice a month.
In other words
Question word + do / does + person + base verb.
do / does stays even with a question word: “Where do you live?” — never “Where you live?”
What · Where · When · Why · Who · What time · How often · How long.
Answers are details, not yes/no: “In Astana.” “At nine.” “Twice a week.”
Notice

Notice: where is do / does in these questions? Tell your partner.

In other words
Question word + do / does + person + base verb.
do / does stays even with a question word: “Where do you live?”
Answers are details, not yes/no: “In Astana.” “At nine.”
Notice

Notice: where is do / does in these questions? Tell your teacher.

In other words
Question word + do / does + person + base verb.
do / does stays even with a question word: “Where do you live?”
Answers are details, not yes/no: “In Astana.” “At nine.”
Stage 6 · Sounds

Sounds

Many weak syllables sound like /ə/ — the “schwa”.

teachER · answER · aGAIN — the weak syllable almost disappears.

Track 3.9 — author, mechanic, pilot, teacherOriginal coursebook recording
Track 3.11 — ten words with a schwaOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
address, after, again, answer, breakfast, clever, daughter, internet, forget, later
1teacher — where is the weak /ə/?
2again — where is the weak /ə/?
3answer — where is the weak /ə/?
4breakfast — the “a” sounds like…
Why

The schwa hides in weak syllables: teacher, again, answer, breakfast.

1later — where is the weak /ə/?
2forget — where is the weak /ə/?
3daughter — where is the weak /ə/?
Why

la-tə · fə-get · daugh-tə — the schwa hides in the weak syllable.

1later — where is the weak /ə/?
2forget — where is the weak /ə/?
3daughter — where is the weak /ə/?
Why

la-tə · fə-get · daugh-tə — the schwa hides in the weak syllable.

Stage 7 · Practice

Practice

Part 1 — Choose the question word.
1___ do you live? — In Almaty.
2___ time does the meeting start? — At ten.
3___ do you live with? — With my parents.
4___ often does she travel? — Twice a month.
5___ do you want to learn English? — Because of my job.
6___ do you take breaks? — At midday.
Why

Where → place · What time / When → time · Who → person · How often → frequency · Why → reason.

1❌ “Where you do live?”
2❌ “What time does she starts work?”
3❌ “Who does live you with?”
Why

Where do you live · does she start (no -s) · Who do you live with.

1___ you work in a team? (now)
2___ she visit the office yesterday?
3Where ___ you go last weekend?
4___ he like his new project? (now)
Why

now → Do / Does · yesterday / last weekend → Did.

1___ does your friend work? — In a hospital.
2___ do you wear to work? — A uniform.
3___ often do you have meetings? — Every Monday.
4___ do they take a break? — At midday.
Why

Where → place · What → thing · How often → frequency · When → time.

1❌ “What time she starts work?”
2❌ “Where do lives your boss?”
3❌ “Why you do want this job?”
Why

What time does she start · Where does your boss live · Why do you want.

1___ your team have a meeting every week? (now)
2Where ___ you work five years ago?
3___ you enjoy the project last month?
Why

now → Does · five years ago / last month → did / Did.

Stage 8 · Listen

Listen

Track 3.3 — two unusual jobsOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
M: I work at a cinema in town, but I don't sell tickets, I'm the piano player! At my cinema they have a lot of old, silent movies so they need someone to play music. I watch the film and decide what type of music to play. If it's a sad part of the film, I play slow music; but if it's an exciting part, I play it fast. — D: I am a 'fire lookout' and I work in a big forest. Fire can be very dangerous here, so my job is to make sure no fires start. I work in a very high tower, so I can see very far. I check the weather on the internet every morning because strong winds can be a big problem. I like my job because the forest is beautiful and quiet.
Track 1.17 — checking phrasesOriginal coursebook recording
Show transcript
Sorry, can you repeat that, please? · How do you spell that? · How do you spell 'russorest'?
Useful language
  • Sorry, can you repeat that?
  • How do you spell that?
  • Do you mean…?
  • So you work at night?
The piano player and the fire lookout — now for the details.

Listen again. Choose the correct answers.

1What music does Máté play for a sad part of the film?
2What does he do first?
3What does Dana check every morning?
4Why does she like her job?
Why

Sad part → slow music. He watches the film and decides. Dana checks the weather — and loves the quiet forest.

1You didn't hear a word. You say:
2You want the letters of a name. You say:
Why

Didn't hear → repeat. Need the letters → spell. Not sure you understood → Do you mean…?

Listen again. Answer the questions.

1What does Máté decide?
2Why does Dana check the weather every morning?
3Where does Dana work?
Why

He decides what music to play · strong winds are dangerous for fires · she works in a high tower.

Stage 9 · Write

Write

Imagine you interview a person with an interesting job.

Write five Wh- questions — and their answers.

Useful language
  • Where do you…?
  • What time do you…?
  • Who do you…?
  • How often do you…?
  • Why do you…?
  • So you…?
Interview your partner — get five details.

Use five different question words. Check what you hear.

Useful language
  • Where do you…?
  • What time do you…?
  • How often do you…?
  • Sorry, can you repeat that?
  • Do you mean…?
  • So you…?
Interview your teacher — get five details.

Use five different question words. Check what you hear.

Useful language
  • Where do you…?
  • What time do you…?
  • How often do you…?
  • Sorry, can you repeat that?
  • Do you mean…?
  • So you…?
In other words
Step 1 — interview your partner about their work or studies: Where…? What time…? Who…? How often…? Why…?
Step 2 — use one checking phrase: “Sorry, can you repeat that?” / “So you…?”
Step 3 — swap. Then tell another pair TWO details about your partner.
In other words
Step 1 — interview your teacher about their work or studies: Where…? What time…? Who…? How often…? Why…?
Step 2 — use one checking phrase: “Sorry, can you repeat that?” / “So you…?”
Step 3 — swap. Then tell your teacher TWO details about your teacher.
Stage 10 · Type it

Type it

Now produce it — type, don’t tap.

Spelling counts. Type the answers, then check.

1___ does your brother work? \u2014 In a bank.
2___ do you spell that?
3___ time does she start? \u2014 At nine.
Why

Question word + does/do + person + base verb: Where does he work?

1What time she start?
2Where does works your brother?
3How you spell that?
Why

Question word + does/do + person + base verb: Where does he work?

1Ask about the place: He works in a bank.
2Ask about the time: She starts at nine.
3Ask them to repeat.
Why

Question word + does/do + person + base verb: Where does he work?
